ui.title: Tool Labels
ui.description: Customize the display names of tool-call bubbles. MCP tools (starting with mcp_) default to “Calling MCP: {mcpDefault}” when not configured. Separate several names with | (e.g. “Writing file|Saving file”) — one is picked at random per call.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.description: Send system notifications when a session reply or a Workflow run completes; clicking a notification jumps to the corresponding content. You are only notified when you have not viewed it yet.
notifications.enableHelp: The system asks for notification permission on the first desktop notification (if denied, enable it manually in System Settings → Notifications → Ginno).
notifications.testHelp: Not affected by the desktop notification toggle; used to verify notification permission and the sound effect.
notifications.testUnavailable: Cannot send a test notification in this environment

floating.title: Floating Window
floating.description: An always-on-top quick chat window: summon it with a global hotkey, with a pill kept on screen and a chat box for quick questions and answers. Full Agent capabilities, with permission confirmations handled inline in the window.
floating.hotkeyWarn: The current hotkey ({hotkey}) failed to register; it may already be used by the system or another app. The menu bar icon can still open the floating window; we recommend recording a new hotkey.
floating.toggleHelp: Same as the menu bar icon’s “Show floating window”; useful for instantly previewing the settings below.
floating.hotkeyHelp: Click the input, then press the key combination (it must include ⌘/⌃/⌥ or be a standalone function key); Esc to cancel. Default {hotkey} — the legacy ⌃⌥Space conflicts with macOS’s “switch input source” shortcut and has been deprecated.
floating.modeFollow: Follow the main window’s current session
floating.defaultModeHelp: You can switch anytime from the title bar dropdown; this setting only decides the initial mode when opened.
floating.opacityHelp: Slide to 1.00 to disable dimming on focus loss.
floating.fsAvoid: Avoid (default): do not cover fullscreen apps
floating.clickThroughHelp: When enabled, the collapsed pill becomes a pure status light and mouse events pass through to the app below (it cannot be clicked to expand; use the hotkey instead).
floating.savedHotkeyConflict: Saved, but the hotkey failed to register — it may already be used by the system or another app. Try a different one.
floating.desktopOnly: Only available in the desktop app
floating.recording: Press the new hotkey… (Esc to cancel)

mcp.title: MCP Servers
mcp.description: {count} servers — tools are injected into every turn; disable unused ones to save tokens.
mcp.reconnectFailedNone: All servers connected — nothing to retry
mcp.enabledToast: Enabled — tools available on the next turn
mcp.disabledToast: Disabled — tools removed on the next turn
mcp.advancedNote: putMcp → reloadMcp — the registry is fully rebuilt. registry.py accepts type or transport; streamable_http spellings are normalized to streamable-http.
mcp.cfgNameNote: Renaming re-registers the server — graph-facing tool names (mcp_<name>_…) and its permission patterns follow the new name.
mcp.cfgTransportNote: registry.py accepts type or transport (Claude-style configs use type); streamable_http / Streamable_HTTP are normalized to streamable-http.
mcp.cfgUrlNote: Gateway URLs carry ?key= auth in the query string.
mcp.cfgHeadersNote: Gateway URLs with ?key= auth need no headers.
mcp.cfgEnvNote: Merged over the parent env (PATH inherited — bundled node/npx resolve).
mcp.toolsNote: Estimate ~130 tokens per enabled tool per turn. Badges come from server annotations (readOnlyHint / destructiveHint); the graph name is what the model and permissions see. A disabled tool is removed from the model entirely — open sessions drop it at the next turn’s graph rebuild.
mcp.toolsUnavailable: Tools unavailable while disconnected — reconnect to refresh the list.
mcp.permsNone: No rules for this server yet.
mcp.permsNote: Synced to settings.json → permissions (allow / ask / deny). Patterns use the mcp_<server>_<tool> namespace with * wildcards.
mcp.activityEmpty: No events observed yet — state changes appear here while this page is open.
mcp.activityFullLog: Client-observed timeline only — full history in ~/.ginno/logs/sidecar.log
mcp.wzOptRemoteDesc: Paste the gateway URL. DingTalk MCP gateway URLs carry ?key= auth in the query string — no headers needed. SSE also supported.
mcp.wzOptStdioDesc: Runs a command on this machine (npx / uvx). Inherits the parent env so bundled node/npx resolve.
mcp.wzPasteLabel: Or paste config JSON (Claude Desktop · Cursor · .mcp.json)
mcp.wzToolsWarn: Tools are injected into every turn — disable unused ones in the Tools tab to save tokens.
mcp.wzTestFailHint: Tip: check the URL and key; a single-line root cause is shown in the server list.
mcp.wzSaved: {name} saved — registry reloaded, tools available on the next turn
mcp.impDetected: Detected: mcpServers format — {count} server(s) — type/transport and spelling auto-normalized on save
mcp.impFail: Could not parse — expected JSON with mcpServers
mcp.impDone: Imported {count} server(s) — saved to mcp.json, connect on next reload
mcp.removeConfirm: Remove “{name}”? {count} tools will disappear from the next turn.
mcp.renameConfirm: Renaming re-registers the server under the new key: graph tool names (mcp_<old>_… → mcp_<new>_…) and its permission patterns change prefix. Old permission patterns are not migrated — clean them up in Security → Permissions.
mcp.advRealNote: Values are shown in plaintext (escape hatch — this local file is readable anyway).
mcp.activityRetry: Lazy retry runs automatically (120s cooldown) — the dot flips green on its own, no action needed.
mcp.empty: No servers yet — click Add Server, or Import JSON to paste an existing config.
mcp.saveFailed: Save failed — is the runtime reachable?
mcp.cfgCorruptTitle: mcp.json is not valid JSON — writes are locked
mcp.cfgCorruptBody: The list shows as empty for now. Toggles, adding and importing are locked so the original config is not overwritten. Paste a corrected full JSON under Advanced below to repair, or fix ~/.ginno/mcp/mcp.json by hand.
mcp.cfgCorruptBlocked: mcp.json is corrupted; writes are locked — repair it under Advanced first
mcp.rollbackFailed: Enable failed and rollback failed too: config stays enabled — retry or disable manually
mcp.reconnectFailedNet: Reconnect request failed — check that the runtime is running

skills.title: Skills
skills.description: One-shot instruction templates (triggered via /<name>). Stored in ~/.ginno/skills/.
skills.importHelp: Point to a skills directory (each subdirectory contains a SKILL.md; lowercase skill.md is also accepted). The whole subdirectory is copied (scripts and reference docs included).
skills.overwriteLabel: Overwrite an existing skill with the same name

agents.title: Agents
agents.description: Per-agent persona / tool subset / model / appearance.
agents.orderNote: The first agent is the default for new sessions. Use the arrows on each card to reorder.
agents.connError: Cannot connect to the runtime (sidecar not started?)
agents.idError: id only supports lowercase letters, digits, - and _, and must start with a letter or digit
agents.iconNote: Leave empty to use the Ginno duck, tinted with this agent's colour.
agents.takeEffectNote: Name / System prompt / tool allowlist / connectors take effect for the next turn of all sessions right after saving.
agents.globsNote: Globs are supported (e.g. mcp_*, todo_*); render / workflow / artifact tools are always available regardless of this list.
agents.connectorsNote: Restricts only this agent (hard rule: not bypassed by tool patterns or skills); the global switch, install and status live on the Connectors page.
agents.subModelsNote: Applies when this agent spawns sub-agents of the listed types (outranks the type's own default); already-running children keep the model they were spawned with.
agents.providerWarn: provider “{provider}” is not enabled; new sessions will fall back to the default ({default})
agents.applyNote: provider / model only apply to sessions created afterwards; color and icon apply immediately (existing sessions keep the icon they were created with).
agents.empty: No agents — the runtime may not be ready yet; after deleting the last agent, the default dev / research / writer are restored automatically.
agents.confirmDelete:
Delete agent “{id}”?
Its memory directory ~/.ginno/agents/{id}/ will not be deleted.
agents.confirmDeleteLast: This is the last agent; after deletion the default dev / research / writer are restored automatically.

workflows.title: Workflows
workflows.description: Multi-step flow recipes (versioned DSL, executed as a LangGraph graph). Click “Details” to view the execution graph / context / logs and trigger runs; for the full two-pane view, see the Workflows page in the left navigation.
workflows.namePlaceholder: name (overrides the name in the DSL)
workflows.dslStepHint: Describe what this step should do here
workflows.mustBeObject: DSL must be a JSON object
workflows.missingNodes: Missing nodes array (at least one node)

synthesis.title: Synthesis Quality
synthesis.description: Success-rate and accuracy funnel for “synthesize into a workflow”. Success rate = first runs completed / total triggered; accuracy relies on case replay and feedback.
synthesis.empty: No records yet. Cases accumulate automatically after you click “synthesize into a workflow” in a chat page.

folders.title: Context Folders
folders.description: Register local folders (repos, notes, docs) into the folder library, then mount them in a session (the TopBar 📁 menu or the /mount command). Once mounted, the Agent can read and write the files directly; AGENTS.md / GINNO.md inside the folder are injected as that folder’s rules.
folders.accessToggleTitle: Click to toggle access level: rw read-write / ro read-only (hard constraint at the tool layer)
folders.confirmRemove: Remove “{name}” from the folder library? Sessions that mounted it will show it as missing.
folders.alreadyRegistered: · already in the library (will be updated)
folders.loadRulesLabel: Load its rule files (AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / GINNO.md)
folders.empty: No folders registered yet. Add one to mount it in sessions.
folders.rulesTooltip: Whether to inject this folder’s AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / GINNO.md into sessions that mount it
folders.securityNote: Security boundary: mounting only grants file access — a folder’s settings / hooks / skills are never loaded (access ≠ config); the read-only level is a hard constraint at the tool layer, independent of Privileged Mode.
folders.autoTooltip: Pre-mount this folder when creating a new session from the home composer

web.title: Web Search
web.enableLabel: Enable built-in web search (web_search / web_fetch tools)
web.searxngHint: Base URL of your self-hosted instance, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8888
web.readAborted: Failed to read existing settings; save aborted (to avoid overwriting other config). Please retry.
web.saved: Saved. Takes effect for new sessions (open sessions keep the tool set they were created with).
web.citationsNote: Search results are registered as sources for the turn, and answers cite them as [sN] per the citation convention; cited sources appear in the “Sources” card under the bubble (🌐 web pages are clickable, 📓 are knowledge-base pages). web_fetch only allows public http/https addresses.

permissions.title: Permissions
permissions.description: Rules look like Tool(arg-glob); the first match wins in deny → ask → allow order, defaulting to ask. This policy is skipped while Privileged Mode is on (see General).

help.allow: Matching rules are allowed without a prompt. e.g. Read(*), Grep(*)
help.ask: Matching rules trigger a confirmation prompt. e.g. Bash(*), Write(*)
help.deny: Matching rules are denied (highest priority). e.g. Bash(rm -rf *)

permissions.loadFailed: Failed to load: runtime not connected
permissions.saved: Saved (takes effect on the next tool call, no restart needed)
permissions.saveFailedConn: Failed to save: runtime not connected

hooks.title: Hooks
hooks.description: Run custom commands on lifecycle events; commands receive a JSON payload on stdin (including event / tool_name, etc.). Hooks always run and are unaffected by Privileged Mode.

help.PreToolUse: Before a tool call; matcher = tool name (e.g. Bash).
help.PostToolUse: After a tool call; matcher = tool name.
help.UserPromptSubmit: When the user submits a message.
help.Stop: At the end of each turn.

hooks.loadFailed: Failed to load: runtime not connected
hooks.saved: Saved (takes effect on the next matching event; hooks are unaffected by Privileged Mode)
hooks.saveFailedConn: Failed to save: runtime not connected

sessionFiles.title: Session Files
sessionFiles.description: Each session owns a dedicated files directory, created automatically with the session; deleting a session only clears the conversation history — the files are kept here for browsing or manual cleanup.
sessionFiles.inUseTitle: Files of an active session are protected and cannot be deleted here; they become cleanable after the session is deleted
sessionFiles.confirmFile: Delete the file “{name}”? It will be removed from disk and cannot be recovered.
sessionFiles.confirmDir: Delete the whole file directory of “{name}”? All files inside will be removed and cannot be recovered. Conversation history is unaffected.

knowledge.title: Knowledge Base
knowledge.description: Point to an Obsidian vault. An existing compiled LLM Wiki (e.g. Molly/Wiki) is indexed directly, no recompilation needed.
knowledge.detected: Detected namespace “{ns}”: Wiki {wiki} pages / Raw {raw} notes
knowledge.noWikiDir: No */Wiki directory detected (the whole vault will be indexed as the knowledge base, {count} notes in total)
knowledge.wikiDir: Wiki directory (searchable knowledge; relative to vault)
knowledge.rawDir: Raw directory (compilation source; relative to vault)
knowledge.autoInject: Auto-inject relevant content into each turn
knowledge.semanticLabel: Semantic retrieval (local embeddings, requires uv sync --extra rag)
knowledge.semanticWeight: Semantic weight (added to the lexical score)
knowledge.semanticNote: When enabled, “Save & Index” / Build wiki embeds the Wiki pages (the model is downloaded on first use). If the rag dependencies are missing, or the model download or encoding fails, it silently falls back to pure lexical retrieval.
knowledge.captureLabel: Capture assistant replies into the memory pool after each turn
knowledge.autoSummarizeLabel: Draft automatically when the threshold is reached (drafts still require manual review; memory is never rewritten silently)
knowledge.distillPlaceholder: Leave empty to use the default provider
knowledge.distillNote: Distillation always produces drafts: review and edit the diff in the right-column Memory panel; only adopted drafts are written to MEMORY.md.

model.title: Model API
model.description: Connect any number of model endpoints: Anthropic protocol, OpenAI-compatible endpoints (DeepSeek / Qwen / Ollama etc.), and the OpenAI Responses API — powering Agent reasoning.
model.connError: Cannot connect to the runtime; the config list is unavailable
model.saveFailedConn: Failed to save: cannot connect to the runtime
model.stillReferenced: Still referenced by: {refs} (rebind the agents / sessions first, then delete)
model.emptyHint: Click “Add config” in the top right, fill in the Base URL and API key, then verify. Anthropic official, DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, local Ollama and other OpenAI-compatible endpoints all work.
model.sysProxyHelp: When on, model requests follow the macOS system proxy settings; when off, all model requests connect directly. Local addresses (127.0.0.1 / localhost) always connect directly. If verification or chat returns 502, your proxy software is usually blocking the local port — try turning this off.
model.defaultTooltip: New sessions use this config by default
model.confirmDefaultPrefix: This config is the global default; after deletion the default switches to the first enabled config.
model.confirmDelete: Delete “{name}”? Agents referencing it will show as deleted, and historical sessions fall back to the default config.

recommendWhy.qwenSearch: Qwen compatible-mode supports server-side web search
recommendWhy.deepseekThinking: DeepSeek supports thinking mode with reasoning output

form.namePlaceholder: e.g. Relay A / DeepSeek / Local Ollama
form.compatHint: OpenAI-compatible endpoints with a custom base_url: DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, relay stations, Ollama, etc.
form.apiKeyLabelOptional: API key (optional; leave empty for local endpoints)
form.bearerAuth: Bearer auth — third-party Anthropic-compatible gateways use Authorization: Bearer instead of x-api-key
form.serverWebSearch: Gateway-side web search — the server runs web_search; no public search engine needed from this machine
form.serverWebSearchHint: Anthropic protocol only. When on, Gin's own web_search tool is withdrawn (the public engines it scrapes are unreachable on restricted networks)
form.orgIdHint: Official OpenAI organization id; only applies to the Responses API
form.enableSearchHint: Web search — requires endpoint support, e.g. Qwen compatible-mode’s enable_search
form.enableThinkingHint: Thinking mode — hybrid thinking models (e.g. Qwen3) output reasoning before the answer; streaming only
form.modelsHint: One model id per line, or comma-separated
form.fetchNeedKeys: Fill in the Base URL and API key to fetch
form.noModelListNote: This provider has no model list yet — enter a model id directly, or add them line by line in the “Model list” field on the left
form.notInListModel: {model} is not in the model list
form.contextWindowHint: Model context window (tokens). Blank = auto (by model name). Reading mods (token-weather) show % of this.
form.stillReferenced: Still referenced by: {refs} (rebind first, then retry)
form.vBaseUrl: An OpenAI Compatible endpoint requires a Base URL.
form.vApiKey: This protocol requires an API key (only compatible endpoints may leave it empty).
form.vModels: Add at least one model id.
form.vDefaultModel: The default model must be one of the models in the list.

usage.title: Usage
usage.subtitle: Global token usage · cache hits · request audit (local records only, retained for 90 days by default)

sessions.footnote: All sessions within the retention period · usage of deleted sessions is kept · click a row to view requests
sessions.rowTitle: View the request log of this session

requests.footnote: One model call per row · counts and metadata only, no request content

overview.loadFailed: Failed to load usage data (runtime not connected?)
overview.windowNote: The stats window only affects this page’s trends and distributions; sessions / request log have their own time filters
overview.empty: Token usage data will appear here once you start chatting.
overview.hitPtNote: pt (cache reads are billed at a discount)
overview.gridPinHint: click to pin · esc to release
overview.gridSplitHelp: Each cell is one two-hour window. The tooltip splits it into cache reads, fresh input and output; the right panel opens out the whole day.
overview.gridPinned: pinned — click the cell again to release
overview.gridAriaLabel: Usage by two-hour bin, one column per day

externalAgents.title: External Agents
externalAgents.intro: Delegate self-contained coding tasks to external coding agent CLIs (claude-code / codex / pi) running one-shot in the workspace.
externalAgents.enableHint: Off by default: delegation spends external vendors' credits and can edit files. Permission posture is fixed per call (read-only default, edit escalates, never a shell).
externalAgents.needsInit: installed but not initialized — run `{name}` once in a terminal to configure a model
externalAgents.ownAccount: Each backend runs with its own CLI config and model account — Ginno never forwards provider credentials.
externalAgents.readAborted: Could not read current settings; save aborted.
externalAgents.maxActiveHint: New delegate calls are rejected while this many are running · saved value takes effect immediately
externalAgents.delegationModeHint: Pin edit / read-only instead of letting the model pick per call · saved value takes effect immediately

mods.title: Mods
mods.intro: Claude Code-compatible mod extensions: each mod runs in its own sandboxed Node process, capabilities gated by grants.
mods.brokerUnavailable: Not connected — broker binary missing or not started
mods.dirHint: Mods are loaded from ~/.ginno/mods/ (drop a mod repo there to install).
mods.noMods: No mods installed. Clone a mod repository into ~/.ginno/mods/ to load it.
mods.grantsHint: Dangerous hook commands (package installs, host settings writes) run only when set to Allow
mods.configHint: JSON · saved to mods.<name>.config, merged over the mod's defaults
mods.compatEmpty: No activity recorded yet this session
